2H.4 Obedience to God required by walking in His ways and by keeping His commandments.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon concerning the blood Joab shed; the doer of evil was rewarded according to his wickedness.
precepts.point: This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart. He did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide; he called them out and they received judgment for taking a man's life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order.
precepts.why:
David was the same at the end of his life. He charged Solomon concerning Joab: “thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace.”

Joab shed blood out of order, in a time of peace, just as Rechab and Baanah slew a righteous person upon his bed. So David said, “Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace.” The doer of evil was rewarded according to his wickedness.

David never let blood shed wickedly slide, not in Ish-bosheth's day and not in Joab's. The same man who slew the messenger in Ziklag, and who hanged Rechab and Baanah over the pool in Hebron, required Joab's blood through his son.

precepts.text: The righteousness of the Most High is everlasting and his law is the truth, the truth in which David's seed was to walk.
precepts.point: There was a stipulation for the throne to continue: if his children take heed to their way and walk before the Most High in truth with all their heart, the throne stands. Reading through the kings, we see many who broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

David charged Solomon to keep the charge of the Lord his God, “to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. And the throne came with a stipulation: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

The truth David’s seed was to walk in is the law. The righteousness of the Most High is everlasting, and his law is the truth. Reading through the kings, many broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous; the throne stood or fell on whether they walked in that truth.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon to be strong, show himself a man, and keep the statutes of the Most High as written in the law of Moses.
precepts.point: The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
David charged Solomon before he died: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. The promise hung on it: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

Solomon did not keep that charge. The kingdom was rent “Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways”, “as did David his father.”

The same charge was then set before Jeroboam: “if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David”. Solomon sought to kill him, and Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

precepts.text: Be strong, show thyself a man, and keep the charge of the Lord to walk in his ways, that thou mayest prosper in all thou doest.
precepts.point: This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.
precepts.why:
David charged Solomon: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself”.

Keeping the charge is what brings the prospering. Hezekiah “wrought that which was good and right and truth before the Lord his God”, sought his God “in the law, and in the commandments”, “and prospered.”

So it is for us: keep his laws and do the work with all your heart, or it will not be blessed.

precepts.text: Keep the charge of the Most High and walk in his ways, and if your children take heed there shall not fail you a man on the throne of Israel.
precepts.point: For the transgression of a land many are its princes, but by a man of understanding and knowledge its state shall be prolonged. That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments; David told Solomon that keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.” That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments.

David told Solomon the same when he charged him: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself”. And the promise tied to it: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

Keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel. That is the man of understanding and knowledge by whom the state of the land is prolonged; transgression multiplies princes, but the commandments keep the throne.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Solomon thrusts out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord, fulfilling the word the Most High spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh. The old judgment on Eli's line is carried out.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Joab, who had turned after Adonijah, flees to the tabernacle of the Lord and catches hold of the horns of the altar, but Solomon sends Benaiah to fall upon him. Joab dies for the innocent blood he shed when he slew Abner and Amasa, two men more righteous and better than he, without David's knowledge.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: The blood returns upon Joab's own head and upon his seed, while upon David and his seed and throne there shall be peace forever from the Lord. Benaiah is set over the host in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Shimei is commanded to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, never crossing the brook Kidron on pain of death, and he agrees. After three years he goes to Gath after his runaway servants and breaks the oath, so Solomon has Benaiah put him to death, and the kingdom is established in Solomon's hand.
